question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Aunt Petunia was ______ a box of after-dinner mints.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. passing around.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence already has the auxiliary “was”, so it needs the present participle (V1+ing) to form the past continuous tense: *was + passing*. (अपूर्ण भूतकाल)

• The phrasal verb pass around means ‘to offer/hand something to each person in a group in turn’ — exactly what one does with a box of mints. (बाँटना)

◦ Correct: Aunt Petunia was passing around a box of after-dinner mints.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “passing round” is a British variant, but with a direct object the standard collocation tested here is “passing around”; “round” is not the preferred option in the key.

• Option 2 “passed around” is a past participle/past form; “was passed around” would be passive and cannot take the object “a box” after it.

• Option 4 “passed away” means ‘to die’, which is completely illogical here.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with “pass”: pass away = die; pass out = faint; pass on = transmit/convey; pass off = pretend to be; pass by = go past.

• Structure: was/were + V1+ing = past continuous (an action in progress in the past).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

As easy as pie
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Very easy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “as easy as pie” means ‘extremely easy, requiring no effort at all’. (बहुत आसान)

◦ It refers to how easy pie is to *eat*, not to bake.

◦ Correct: The last question in the paper was as easy as pie, so everyone attempted it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “Tasteful” (रुचिपूर्ण) relates to good taste/aesthetics — a trap based on the word “pie”.

• Option 2 “Auspicious” (शुभ) means favourable or promising — unrelated.

• Option 4 “Difficult choice” is the opposite of the idiom’s meaning.

NOTE

• Similar idioms meaning ‘very easy’: a piece of cake, a walk in the park, child’s play, as easy as ABC, duck soup.

• Related idiom: pie in the sky = an unrealistic hope or plan.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A state of agitation especially over a trivial matter
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fuss.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fuss (noun) = unnecessary excitement, worry or activity, especially about something unimportant. (छोटी बात पर हंगामा)

◦ The key element in the definition is “especially over a trivial matter”, which exactly matches “fuss”.

◦ Correct: She made a fuss about the seating arrangement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “Storm” (तूफान) is a violent weather disturbance or a serious outburst — it does not carry the ‘trivial’ sense.

• Option 2 “Harmony” (सामंजस्य) means peaceful agreement — the opposite.

• Option 3 “Worry” (चिंता) is anxiety about a real problem, not a noisy show over something petty.

NOTE

• Useful phrases: make a fuss over/about = complain noisily; kick up a fuss = protest loudly; fussy = hard to please.

• Related one-word substitutions: Tempest in a teapot = a big commotion over a small matter.

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct Idiom for the bracketed text.

That’s just like Julie – always (coming to conclusions too quickly) even before she knows the facts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. jumping in with both feet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jump in with both feet means ‘to enter into something hastily and without thinking it through’ — i.e. to act or judge too quickly. (बिना सोचे कूद पड़ना)

◦ It fits the bracketed idea of forming conclusions “before she knows the facts”.

◦ Correct: That’s just like Julie – always jumping in with both feet even before she knows the facts.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “raring to go” = very eager and enthusiastic to start — it shows eagerness, not hasty judgement.

• Option 3 “in the same boat” = sharing the same difficult situation — irrelevant here.

• Option 4 “bite one’s tongue” = to stop oneself from speaking — the exact opposite of acting hastily.

NOTE

• Closely related idiom: jump to conclusions = to judge before knowing all the facts.

• Other ‘foot’ idioms: put one’s foot in the mouth = say something tactless; get cold feet = lose courage; stand on one’s own feet = be independent.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

I wanted to ______ things that girls weren’t supposed to do.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. do a lot of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After “to” (to-infinitive) we always use the base form V1, hence “to do”, not “to done”. (मूल क्रिया रूप)

• The quantifier is written as three separate words: a lot of + plural/uncountable noun (“things”). (बहुत सारे)

◦ Correct: I wanted to do a lot of things that girls weren’t supposed to do.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “do allot of” — “allot” is a verb meaning ‘to distribute/assign’ and cannot act as a quantifier.

• Option 2 “done a lot of” wrongly puts the past participle V3 after “to”.

• Option 3 “do a lot off” confuses the preposition “of” with the adverb/preposition “off”.

NOTE

• Confusables: a lot (many) vs allot (to assign) vs alot (not a word); of (belonging to) vs off (away from).

• “A lot of / lots of” works with both countable and uncountable nouns; “many” only with countable and “much” only with uncountable.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

If I was your sister, I would have never slapped you.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. If I was your.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence expresses an imaginary/unreal condition, so it needs the subjunctive mood: with “if” in an unreal situation we use were with every subject, including I/he/she/it. (अवास्तविक स्थिति)

◦ Rule: If + subject + were ..., subject + would + V1 (Type 2 conditional).

◦ Correct: If I were your sister, I would have never slapped you.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “never slapped you.” is correct — the adverb “never” is properly placed after the auxiliary “have”.

• Option 3 “sister, I would have” is grammatically fine as printed.

• Option 4 “No error” is wrong because the segment “If I was” does contain an error.

NOTE

• Subjunctive ‘were’ is also used after wish, as if / as though, if only, suppose: *I wish I were rich*; *He talks as if he were the boss*.

• With a real/factual past condition, ‘was’ is acceptable: *If he was at home, he must have heard the bell.*

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

His gray, lifeless eyes were sunken.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. vibrant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lifeless means dull, without energy, spiritless or dead. (निर्जीव)

• Vibrant means full of energy, life and brightness — the exact opposite. (ओजस्वी / चमकदार)

◦ Correct: His gray, lifeless eyes were sunken. → antonym of “lifeless” = vibrant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “extinct” (विलुप्त) = no longer in existence — a synonym-side word, not an antonym.

• Option 2 “lapsed” (समाप्त हो चुका) = expired or no longer valid — also close to ‘lifeless’ in sense.

• Option 4 “pointed” (नुकीला) = sharp or direct — unrelated to liveliness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lifeless: inert, insipid, dull, listless, inanimate.

• Synonyms of vibrant: lively, spirited, animated, dynamic, energetic.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She ______ and left the room, carefully pulling the door shut.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sighed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a past-tense verb parallel to “left” (She ____ and left). Only “sighed” is a past-tense verb. (आह भरना)

• Sigh = to let out a long, deep breath expressing sadness, relief or tiredness — which suits someone quietly leaving a room.

◦ Correct: She sighed and left the room, carefully pulling the door shut.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “site” (स्थल) is a noun meaning a place or location.

• Option 3 “side” (पक्ष/किनारा) is a noun and cannot be joined to “left” by “and”.

• Option 4 “slide” is present tense, breaking parallelism with “left” (the past form would be “slid”).

NOTE

• Homophone alert: site (place) / sight (vision) / cite (to quote).

• Parallelism rule: verbs joined by and/or/but must be in the same form and tense.

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: It turns out multiple groups have measured the concensus.
option_2: The proposed cuts have caused considerable contraversy.
option_3: The companies may lose a lot of their overseas exposure.
option_4: She was in a bouyant mood and was looking forward to her new life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The companies may lose a lot of their overseas exposure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 3 — *companies, lose, overseas, exposure* — is spelt correctly, so it is the error-free sentence.

• Note “lose” (खोना, verb) is spelt with one ‘o’, unlike “loose” (ढीला, adjective).

◦ Correct: The companies may lose a lot of their overseas exposure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: “concensus” is wrong → correct spelling is consensus (सर्वसम्मति).

• Option 2: “contraversy” is wrong → correct spelling is controversy (विवाद).

• Option 4: “bouyant” is wrong → correct spelling is buoyant (उत्साहपूर्ण / उतराने वाला).

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt SSC words: occurrence, accommodation, embarrass, maintenance, privilege, questionnaire, liaison, millennium.

• Remember: consensus comes from ‘consent’ (not ‘census’), so there is no ‘c’ in the middle.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Impertinent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Polite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Impertinent means rude, disrespectful or impudent, especially towards someone senior. (धृष्ट / अशिष्ट)

• Polite means showing good manners and respect — the exact opposite. (विनम्र)

◦ Correct: His impertinent reply annoyed the teacher; a polite answer was expected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “Irrelevant” (अप्रासंगिक) is close to the *other* sense of impertinent (‘not pertinent’), so it is a synonym, not an antonym.

• Option 3 “Insolent” (गुस्ताख) is a direct synonym of impertinent — the classic trap.

• Option 4 “Personal” (व्यक्तिगत) is unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of impertinent: impudent, insolent, brazen, cheeky, saucy, presumptuous.

• Antonyms: polite, courteous, respectful, deferential, civil.

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed part given in the sentence below.

The women stared at me with (great interest or concern).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. curiosity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Curiosity = a strong desire to know or learn something; keen interest in something. (जिज्ञासा)

• It matches the bracketed phrase “great interest or concern” and collocates naturally with “stared at me with”.

◦ Correct: The women stared at me with curiosity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “intellect” (बुद्धि) is the power of reasoning, not interest.

• Option 2 “control” (नियंत्रण) means power over something — unrelated.

• Option 4 “possession” (अधिकार/संपत्ति) means ownership — unrelated.

NOTE

• Word family: curious (adj.), curiously (adv.), curiosity (noun).

• Idiom: Curiosity killed the cat — being too inquisitive can get one into trouble.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Capricious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Arbitrary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Capricious means given to sudden, unpredictable changes of mood or behaviour; whimsical. (सनकी / अस्थिरमति)

• Arbitrary means based on random choice or personal whim rather than on reason — hence the closest synonym. (मनमाना)

◦ Correct: The manager’s capricious (arbitrary) decisions confused the whole team.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “Stable” (स्थिर) means firm and unchanging — an antonym.

• Option 3 “Steadfast” (अटल) means firmly loyal and unwavering — also an antonym.

• Option 4 “Cautious” (सावधान) means careful — unrelated to unpredictability.

NOTE

• Synonyms of capricious: fickle, whimsical, mercurial, erratic, volatile, impulsive.

• Antonyms: constant, consistent, steady, predictable, resolute.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate choice.

In more civilized times even the most ______ enemies were treated with dignity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. implacable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Implacable means unable to be appeased or pacified; relentlessly hostile. (अटल शत्रुता रखने वाला)

• “Implacable enemies” is a standard collocation, and the contrast with “treated with dignity” makes the sense of bitter hostility fit perfectly.

◦ Correct: In more civilized times even the most implacable enemies were treated with dignity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “explicable” (समझाया जा सकने योग्य) = able to be explained — meaningless with ‘enemies’.

• Option 2 “vindicable” = able to be justified or defended — does not suit ‘most ___ enemies’.

• Option 4 “ineducable” = incapable of being educated — illogical in this context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of implacable: unappeasable, inexorable, unrelenting, merciless, remorseless.

• Antonyms: placable, merciful, lenient, forgiving. Related word: placate = to calm someone’s anger.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option ‘no correction required’ if the sentence is correct as given.

Welcome to the Ministry of Magic, (please administer your name) and business.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. please state your name.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb state means ‘to declare or say something formally/clearly’, which is exactly what a reception desk asks a visitor to do. (बताना / घोषित करना)

• “State your name and business” is a fixed, idiomatic security/reception expression.

◦ Correct: Welcome to the Ministry of Magic, please state your name and business.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “No correction required” is wrong because “administer” (= to manage or dispense) cannot take ‘your name’ as an object.

• Option 2 “please direct your name” is illogical — “direct” means to guide or aim, not to declare.

• Option 4 “please inform your entitle” is ungrammatical; “entitle” is a verb, not a noun.

NOTE

• Confusables: administer (manage/give out) vs administrate; title (noun) vs entitle (verb, to give a right/name).

• Collocations with ‘state’: state your case, state the facts, state your intentions.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ubiquitous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is u-b-i-q-u-i-t-o-u-s; note that in English ‘q’ is always followed by ‘u’.

• Ubiquitous (adj.) = present or found everywhere at the same time. (सर्वव्यापी)

◦ Correct: Mobile phones have become ubiquitous in modern life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “ubiqitous” drops the compulsory ‘u’ after ‘q’.

• Option 2 “ubquitous” omits the ‘i’ after ‘ub’.

• Option 4 “ubiqoitous” wrongly replaces ‘u’ with ‘o’ after ‘q’.

NOTE

• Noun form: ubiquity; synonyms: omnipresent, pervasive, universal, everywhere.

• Other ‘qu’ spellings often asked: acquaintance, conquer, liquefy, questionnaire, eloquent.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

The 1918 influenza pandemic sweep the world within months.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. pandemic sweep the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a completed past event (1918), so the verb must be in the simple past tense: “swept”, not “sweep”. (भूतकाल)

◦ “Sweep” is an irregular verb: sweep – swept – swept.

◦ Correct: The 1918 influenza pandemic swept the world within months.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “No error” is wrong because the verb form is clearly incorrect.

• Option 2 “world within months.” is correct — “within” properly expresses a period of time.

• Option 4 “The 1918 influenza” is a correctly formed noun phrase with the definite article.

NOTE

• Even if the subject were singular present, it would need “sweeps” — “pandemic sweep” violates subject-verb agreement as well.

• Similar irregular verbs: keep–kept, sleep–slept, creep–crept, weep–wept, sweep–swept.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option ‘no correction required’ if the sentence is correct as given.

The relationship between two people is (by the way in what) they feel and behave towards each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the way in which.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the linking verb “is” we need a noun phrase as the complement, so “the way” must follow, not the preposition “by”.

• The noun “way” takes the relative structure “in which” (or simply “that/Ø”), never “in what”. (रीति जिसमें)

◦ Correct: The relationship between two people is the way in which they feel and behave towards each other.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “the way by which” uses the wrong preposition — we say *the way in which*, not *by which*, for manner.

• Option 2 “by which ways” leaves the sentence without a complement for “is” and is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 “No correction required” is wrong because “in what” cannot introduce a relative clause after ‘way’.

NOTE

• Rule: what is not a relative pronoun after a stated antecedent; use which/that/who.

• Acceptable variants: *the way they behave*, *the way that they behave*, *the manner in which they behave*.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.

He best understand that / because of the fight it is no / longer his decision to make.
option_3: because of the fight it is no
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. He best understand that.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With the third-person singular subject “He” in the simple present tense, the verb must take -s: “understands”. (कर्ता-क्रिया मेल)

• Also, “best” is the superlative of ‘well’; the natural adverb here is “better than anyone” / “best of all”, but the tested error is the verb form.

◦ Correct: He understands that because of the fight it is no longer his decision to make.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “longer his decision to make.” correctly completes the phrase “no longer”.

• Option 3 “because of the fight it is no” is correct — “because of” is rightly followed by a noun phrase.

• Option 4 “No error” is wrong because the first segment violates subject-verb agreement.

NOTE

• Rule: He/She/It + V1 + s/es in simple present; I/We/You/They + V1.

• “Because of” (preposition) + noun; “because” (conjunction) + clause.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’.

Besides the atmospheric changes that make us sweat, (hormonal or emotional stimulus can also cause sweating).
option_1: hormonal and emotional stimuli also causes sweating
option_2: hormonal or emotional stimuli can also cause sweating
option_4: hormonal or emotional stimulus also causing sweating
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. hormonal or emotional stimuli can also cause sweating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence talks about causes in general, so the plural noun “stimuli” (singular: *stimulus*) is required, and it takes the plural verb “cause”. (उत्तेजक)

• The modal “can” is always followed by the bare infinitive (V1) — “can also cause”.

◦ Correct: Besides the atmospheric changes that make us sweat, hormonal or emotional stimuli can also cause sweating.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses “stimuli also causes” — a plural subject cannot take the singular verb ‘causes’.

• Option 3 “No substitution required” is wrong: the printed singular “stimulus” does not fit the general plural sense intended.

• Option 4 “stimulus also causing sweating” has no finite verb, making the clause incomplete.

NOTE

• Latin plurals often asked: stimulus–stimuli, radius–radii, criterion–criteria, phenomenon–phenomena, datum–data, syllabus–syllabi.

• Modals (can, may, must, should, will) are always followed by V1 without ‘to’.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Sets of principles concerned with the nature and appreciation of beauty
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Aesthetics.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aesthetics is the branch of philosophy dealing with the nature of beauty, art and taste. (सौंदर्यशास्त्र)

• The definition’s key words — “principles” + “appreciation of beauty” — point directly to aesthetics.

◦ Correct: The design of the building was praised for its aesthetics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “Asylum” (शरण/पागलखाना) = shelter/protection given to refugees, or an institution for the mentally ill.

• Option 3 “Atonement” (प्रायश्चित) = making amends for a wrong or sin.

• Option 4 “Aspersion” (लांछन) = a damaging or false remark about someone’s character.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: Ethics = principles of right and wrong; Epistemology = study of knowledge; Metaphysics = study of the nature of reality.

• Idiom: cast aspersions on = to criticise or slander someone.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Louisiana hosts one of the (1) ________ well known celebrations - Mardi Gras. Mardi Gras is French for “Fat Tuesday”. This (2) ________ is sometimes called “Shrove Tuesday”. (3) ________ wear masks and costumes, overturn social conventions, dance, organize competitions and parades. Related popular practices (4) ________ associated with celebrations before the fasting and religious obligations associated (5) ________ the penitential season of Lent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. most.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure is “one of the + superlative + plural noun”, so a superlative degree word is needed before “well known celebrations”. (सबसे अधिक)

• Most forms the superlative of long adjectives: *most well known* = the best known of all.

◦ Correct: Louisiana hosts one of the most well known celebrations – Mardi Gras.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “all” cannot precede an adjective in this pattern (“one of the all well known” is ungrammatical).

• Option 2 “some” is a quantifier and does not create the required superlative sense.

• Option 4 “more” is comparative and needs “than”; “one of the more...” weakens the intended sense of highest degree.

NOTE

• Degrees: well known – more well known (better known) – most well known (best known).

• Fixed pattern: one of the + superlative + plural noun + singular verb.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Louisiana hosts one of the (1) ________ well known celebrations - Mardi Gras. Mardi Gras is French for “Fat Tuesday”. This (2) ________ is sometimes called “Shrove Tuesday”. (3) ________ wear masks and costumes, overturn social conventions, dance, organize competitions and parades. Related popular practices (4) ________ associated with celebrations before the fasting and religious obligations associated (5) ________ the penitential season of Lent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. holiday.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank refers back to Mardi Gras / “Fat Tuesday”, which is a single festive day; such a day is called a holiday. (अवकाश का दिन/पर्व)

• “Shrove Tuesday” is likewise the name of a religious holiday, so “holiday” fits the definition sentence perfectly.

◦ Correct: This holiday is sometimes called “Shrove Tuesday”.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 “variation” (भिन्नता) means a change or difference — illogical.

• Option 3 “vacation” (छुट्टी की अवधि) is a longer period away from work/school, not a single named day.

• Option 4 “vocation” (व्यवसाय/बुलावा) means a career or calling — unrelated.

NOTE

• Confusables: vacation (holiday period) / vocation (profession) / avocation (hobby).

• Mardi Gras (French for “Fat Tuesday”) is celebrated the day before Ash Wednesday, which begins Lent.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Louisiana hosts one of the (1) ________ well known celebrations - Mardi Gras. Mardi Gras is French for “Fat Tuesday”. This (2) ________ is sometimes called “Shrove Tuesday”. (3) ________ wear masks and costumes, overturn social conventions, dance, organize competitions and parades. Related popular practices (4) ________ associated with celebrations before the fasting and religious obligations associated (5) ________ the penitential season of Lent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. People.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verbs that follow — wear masks and costumes, overturn social conventions, dance, organize competitions and parades — can only be performed by human beings. (लोग)

• “People” is a plural subject, so it agrees with the plural verb “wear”.

◦ Correct: People wear masks and costumes, overturn social conventions, dance, organize competitions and parades.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “Plants” cannot wear costumes or dance — contextually absurd.

• Option 3 “Animals” do not organize competitions or overturn social conventions.

• Option 4 “Birds” is equally illogical for the listed human activities.

NOTE

• “People” is a plural noun and always takes a plural verb: *People are waiting.*

• “Peoples” (with -s) is used only for different nations/ethnic groups: *the peoples of Asia*.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Louisiana hosts one of the (1) ________ well known celebrations - Mardi Gras. Mardi Gras is French for “Fat Tuesday”. This (2) ________ is sometimes called “Shrove Tuesday”. (3) ________ wear masks and costumes, overturn social conventions, dance, organize competitions and parades. Related popular practices (4) ________ associated with celebrations before the fasting and religious obligations associated (5) ________ the penitential season of Lent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. were.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject is the plural noun phrase “Related popular practices”, so the verb must be plural: were. (बहुवचन क्रिया)

• The structure needed is the passive be + past participle: *were associated with*.

◦ Correct: Related popular practices were associated with celebrations before the fasting ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “will be” shifts the passage into the future, which clashes with the descriptive/historical tone.

• Option 2 “have” would need “been” (“have been associated”) to be grammatical here.

• Option 4 “is” is singular and cannot agree with the plural subject “practices”.

NOTE

• Passive voice: subject + be (is/are/was/were) + V3 (past participle) + by/with.

• Subject-verb agreement: identify the head noun (“practices”), not the nearest modifier.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Louisiana hosts one of the (1) ________ well known celebrations - Mardi Gras. Mardi Gras is French for “Fat Tuesday”. This (2) ________ is sometimes called “Shrove Tuesday”. (3) ________ wear masks and costumes, overturn social conventions, dance, organize competitions and parades. Related popular practices (4) ________ associated with celebrations before the fasting and religious obligations associated (5) ________ the penitential season of Lent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb “associate” takes the fixed preposition with: *associated with something*. (के साथ जुड़ा हुआ)

• The same collocation already appears earlier in the passage: “associated with celebrations”.

◦ Correct: ... religious obligations associated with the penitential season of Lent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “from” indicates origin or separation — wrong with ‘associated’.

• Option 3 “of” shows possession and does not collocate with ‘associated’.

• Option 4 “off” means away from a surface — wholly unsuitable.

NOTE

• Fixed prepositions: associated with, acquainted with, familiar with, connected with/to, linked to.

• Lent is the 40-day penitential season observed by Christians before Easter, beginning on Ash Wednesday.

question: India shares longest land border with which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bangladesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's total land boundary is about 15,106.7 km, and the longest stretch is shared with Bangladesh — about 4,096.7 km. (सीमा — boundary)

• The Indian states touching Bangladesh are West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; West Bengal has the longest share.

• The India–Bangladesh boundary was settled by the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA), 2015 (100th Constitutional Amendment), which exchanged enclaves.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• China — about 3,488 km (the McMahon Line / Line of Actual Control), second longest.

• Pakistan — about 3,323 km, marked by the Radcliffe Line (1947).

• Nepal — about 1,751 km, an open border under the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship.

NOTE

• Order of India's land borders (longest to shortest): Bangladesh > China > Pakistan > Nepal > Myanmar (1,643 km) > Bhutan (699 km) > Afghanistan (106 km).

• Rajasthan has the longest border with Pakistan among Indian states; Arunachal Pradesh has the longest with China.

question: Pongal is another name for Makar Sankranti, which is celebrated during the same time in various cities of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pongal is the four-day harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, celebrated in the Tamil month of Thai (mid-January), at the same time as Makar Sankranti. (फ़सल कटाई का त्योहार — harvest festival)

• The four days are Bhogi, Thai Pongal (Surya Pongal), Mattu Pongal (cattle worship) and Kaanum Pongal.

• The festival marks the northward journey of the Sun (Uttarayan) and thanksgiving to the Sun God, cattle and farm labour.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Andhra Pradesh/Telangana — the same festival is celebrated as Sankranti with Bhogi and Kanuma.

• Karnataka — celebrated as Suggi/Makara Sankranti with 'Ellu Bella' exchange.

• Kerala — the major festivals are Onam (harvest) and Vishu, not Pongal.

NOTE

• Same-day harvest festivals: Lohri (Punjab), Magh/Bhogali Bihu (Assam), Uttarayan (Gujarat), Poush Parbon (West Bengal), Khichdi (UP/Bihar), Shishur Saenkraat (Kashmir).

• Makar Sankranti is one of the few Indian festivals fixed to the solar calendar (14/15 January).

question: Which among the following is a cooking procedure in which the sugar in the food gets oxidized, turning into a brown colour?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Caramelisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Caramelisation is the non-enzymatic browning of sugar on heating, in which sugar molecules break down and oxidise to give a brown colour and nutty flavour. (शर्करा का भूरा होना)

• Sucrose caramelises at about 160–170 °C; it is used in making caramel, toffee, jaggery sweets and browning of baked goods.

• It is different from the Maillard reaction, which needs both a reducing sugar and an amino acid/protein (as in bread crust and roasted meat).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Filtration — separating an insoluble solid from a liquid using a filter, e.g. straining tea.

• Emulsification — mixing two immiscible liquids (oil and water) into a stable mixture, e.g. mayonnaise; bile emulsifies fat in our body.

• Bromination — a chemical reaction adding bromine to a compound; it is not a cooking process.

NOTE

• Browning types: Caramelisation (sugar only), Maillard (sugar + protein), enzymatic browning (polyphenol oxidase, as in cut apples/potatoes).

• Common cooking chemistry asked in SSC: denaturation of protein on boiling an egg, gelatinisation of starch.

question: After recovering from an infectious illness, often small pox, Brita dance is typically performed to thank the local deity. It is one of the most well-known dances of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Brita (also spelt Brata/Vrita) dance is a folk dance of West Bengal, performed as a vow (vrata) of thanksgiving to the local deity after recovery from an infectious disease such as small pox, or on fulfilment of a wish. (व्रत नृत्य)

• It is usually performed by women and is closely tied to village deity worship, especially Shitala, the goddess associated with small pox.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other West Bengal folk dances — Chhau (Purulia), Gambhira, Domni, Baul, Kathi, Dhali, Alkap, Santhali.

• Bihar — Jat-Jatin, Bidesia, Jhijhian, Paika, Karma.

• Uttar Pradesh — Kathak (classical), Charkula, Raslila, Nautanki, Jhora.

• Jharkhand — Chhau (Seraikela), Paika, Jhumar, Karma, Domkach.

NOTE

• Chhau dance (Purulia–Seraikela–Mayurbhanj) was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

• Classical dance of West Bengal region — Gaudiya Nritya; the state's famous theatre form is Jatra.

question: Which country is the only country in the world to have both tigers and lions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India is the only country in the world where both lions and tigers are found in the wild. (एकमात्र देश जहाँ शेर और बाघ दोनों हैं)

• The Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica) survives only in the Gir forest of Gujarat — Gir National Park and the Barda/Girnar landscape.

• The Royal Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris tigris) is the National Animal of India and is spread over 50+ tiger reserves.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kenya and South Africa have African lions, leopards and cheetahs but no tigers in the wild.

• China historically had tigers (Siberian/South China tiger) but no wild lions.

• India is also the only country with lion, tiger, leopard, snow leopard and clouded leopard — five big cats.

NOTE

• Project Tiger — 1973 (started at Jim Corbett); Project Elephant — 1992; Asiatic Lion Conservation Project — 2018.

• Tiger census is done every 4 years by the NTCA + Wildlife Institute of India; the 2022 estimate was 3,682 tigers.

question: “Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas” is observed on the birth anniversary of ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birsa Munda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas (Tribal Pride Day) is observed every year on 15 November, the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda (born 15 November 1875). (जनजातीय गौरव दिवस)

• The Union Cabinet declared the day in November 2021 to honour the contribution of tribal freedom fighters.

• Birsa Munda led the Ulgulan (Great Tumult) / Munda rebellion (1899–1900) against the British and the dikus in the Chhotanagpur region; he is revered as 'Dharti Aaba' (Father of the Earth).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mahatma Gandhi — birth anniversary 2 October, observed as Gandhi Jayanti and International Day of Non-Violence.

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel — 31 October, observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day).

• B. R. Ambedkar — 14 April, observed as Ambedkar Jayanti / Samvidhan Nirmata Diwas.

NOTE

• Birsa Munda's movement led to the Chhotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, which protected tribal land rights.

• 15 November is also the foundation day of Jharkhand (2000).

question: Which Odissi dancer was the first dancer of foreign origin to be conferred the Padma Shri in 2006?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ileana Citaristi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ileana Citaristi, an Italian-born Odissi and Mayurbhanj Chhau dancer settled in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, was awarded the Padma Shri in 2006 — the first dancer of foreign origin to receive it. (पद्म श्री)

• She learnt Odissi from Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and Mayurbhanj Chhau from Guru Hari Nayak, and founded the Art Vision dance academy.

• Odissi is a classical dance of Odisha, based on the Natya Shastra and the sculptures of the Konark and Jagannath temples.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mrinalini Sarabhai — Indian Bharatanatyam/Kathakali dancer, founder of Darpana Academy, Padma Shri 1965 and Padma Bhushan 1992.

• Sofia Boutella — Algerian-French dancer and film actress, not connected with Odissi.

• Eri Nakamura — a Japanese opera singer, not an Odissi dancer.

NOTE

• Eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Padma awards are announced on Republic Day (26 January) every year.

question: Which of the following singer is honoured with the Padma Shri 2022 by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonu Nigam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Playback singer Sonu Nigam was conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 in the field of Art (Music). (पद्म श्री — 2022)

• He is known for songs such as *Kal Ho Naa Ho*, *Suraj Hua Maddham*, *Sandese Aate Hain*, and won the National Film Award for Best Male Playback Singer (2003) for 'Kal Ho Naa Ho'.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award of India, after Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Abhijeet Bhattacharya, Anu Malik and Leslie Lewis are well-known figures of Indian film and pop music but have not received the Padma Shri.

• Other music-related Padma awardees of 2022: Sandhya Mukherjee (Padma Shri, declined) and Rashid Khan (Padma Bhushan, 2022).

NOTE

• Order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri; instituted in 1954.

• The Bharat Ratna 2022 was not awarded; Padma Vibhushan 2022 went to Kalyan Singh (posthumous), Radheshyam Khemka (posthumous), General Bipin Rawat (posthumous), Prabha Atre.

question: The Mahabodhi Temple Complex has direct association with the life of the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Buddha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya (Bihar) marks the spot where Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment (nirvana/bodhi) under the Bodhi (peepal) tree. (ज्ञान प्राप्ति स्थल)

• The first temple here was built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; the present brick structure largely dates to the Gupta period (5th–6th century CE).

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002 and is one of the four holiest Buddhist sites.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jain sites — Dilwara (Mt. Abu), Palitana (Gujarat), Shravanabelagola (Karnataka), Ranakpur (Rajasthan).

• Mughal monuments — Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Humayun's Tomb.

• Sikh Gurus — associated with Harmandir Sahib (Amritsar), Anandpur Sahib, Patna Sahib, Nanded.

NOTE

• Four great events in Buddha's life and their places: Birth — Lumbini (Nepal); Enlightenment — Bodh Gaya; First Sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) — Sarnath; Mahaparinirvana — Kushinagar.

• Their symbols: lotus/bull, Bodhi tree, wheel, stupa respectively.

question: If we deduct depreciation from GNP the measure of aggregate income that we obtain is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Net National Product.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NNP = GNP − Depreciation (consumption of fixed capital). Removing depreciation converts a 'gross' measure into a 'net' measure. (मूल्यह्रास — depreciation)

• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA); so NNP measures the net output produced by a country's normal residents in a year.

• NNP at factor cost is called National Income; NNP at market price = NNP at FC + net indirect taxes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) — value of final goods and services produced within the domestic territory, before deducting depreciation.

• National income technically means NNP at factor cost, not the direct result of GNP minus depreciation at market prices.

• Private income — income accruing to the private sector from all sources, including transfer payments and interest on public debt.

NOTE

• Key formulae: NDP = GDP − Depreciation; GNP = GDP + NFIA; NNP = GNP − Depreciation.

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI; the current base year is 2011–12.

question: The Union Finance Ministry issued a notification amending the Electoral Bonds Scheme to allow the sale of electoral bonds for extra ______ days in the year of general elections to the Legislative Assembly of States and UTs with legislature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2022, the Union Finance Ministry amended the Electoral Bonds Scheme, 2018 to permit an additional period of 15 days for the sale of electoral bonds in the year of general elections to the Legislative Assembly of States and Union Territories with legislature. (चुनावी बॉण्ड)

• Normally, electoral bonds were sold in four windows of 10 days each in January, April, July and October, with an extra 30 days in the year of Lok Sabha general elections.

• Electoral bonds were interest-free bearer instruments sold only by the State Bank of India (SBI) in denominations of ₹1,000 to ₹1 crore.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A political party could encash the bond only through an authorised bank account and only if it had secured at least 1% of votes in the last general election.

• The scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2017–18 and notified on 2 January 2018.

NOTE

• The Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bonds Scheme as unconstitutional on 15 February 2024, holding that it violated the right to information under Article 19(1)(a).

• Election-funding bodies to remember: Election Commission of India (Article 324), and disclosure norms under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

question: Who is the author of the novel, "Oliver Twist"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Charles Dickens.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Oliver Twist' (1838) is a novel by the English writer Charles Dickens, about an orphan boy in London's workhouses and criminal underworld. (उपन्यासकार — novelist)

• Dickens is famous for exposing the social evils of Victorian England — poverty, child labour and the workhouse system.

• Other novels by Dickens: A Tale of Two Cities, Great Expectations, David Copperfield, Hard Times, Bleak House, The Pickwick Papers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Mark Twain (American) — *The Adventures of Tom Sawyer*, *The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn*.

• Oscar Wilde (Irish) — *The Picture of Dorian Gray*, *The Importance of Being Earnest*.

• Jane Austen — *Pride and Prejudice*, *Sense and Sensibility*, *Emma*, *Mansfield Park*.

NOTE

• Famous opening line of *A Tale of Two Cities*: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.'

• Frequently asked author–book pairs: Charles Dickens — Oliver Twist; Leo Tolstoy — War and Peace; Victor Hugo — Les Misérables; George Orwell — Animal Farm.

question: Judo has its origin in ancient ______ art of Ju-jitsu.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Japanese.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Judo originated from the ancient Japanese martial art of Ju-jitsu (Jujutsu). (जूडो — जापानी मार्शल आर्ट)

• Modern Judo was founded by Jigoro Kano in 1882, when he established the Kodokan school in Tokyo; 'Judo' means 'the gentle way'.

• Judo became an Olympic sport at the 1964 Tokyo Games (women's judo added at Barcelona 1992).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Karate, Sumo, Kendo, Aikido and Ju-jitsu are also Japanese martial arts.

• Taekwondo is from Korea; Kung Fu / Wushu / Tai Chi are from China; Silat is practised in Malaysia and Indonesia.

NOTE

• Judo terms: contest area tatami, uniform judogi, full point Ippon, half point Waza-ari.

• Indian martial arts: Kalaripayattu (Kerala), Silambam (Tamil Nadu), Thang-Ta (Manipur), Gatka (Punjab), Mardani Khel (Maharashtra).

question: The slash and burn agriculture is called ‘Bewar’ or ‘Dahiya’ in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Slash-and-burn (shifting) cultivation is known as 'Bewar' or 'Dahiya' in Madhya Pradesh. (झूम/स्थानांतरी कृषि)

• In this system, forest patches are cleared and burnt, crops are grown on the ash-enriched soil for 2–3 years, and the plot is then abandoned for regeneration.

• It is practised mainly by tribal communities on hill slopes and results in soil erosion and loss of fertility.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Odisha — the same practice is called 'Podu' (also in Andhra Pradesh) and 'Koman/Bringa'.

• Assam and the North-East — it is called 'Jhum', the best-known Indian name for shifting cultivation.

• Uttar Pradesh (Himalayan belt) — it is called 'Khil'.

NOTE

• Other Indian names: Penda/Beera (Chhattisgarh–MP), Kumari (Western Ghats), Valre or Waltre (South-East Rajasthan), Kuruwa (Jharkhand).

• Global names: Milpa (Mexico/Central America), Ladang (Indonesia/Malaysia), Ray (Vietnam), Chena (Sri Lanka), Roca (Brazil).

question: Who gave title of “Father of the Nation” to Mahatma Gandhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Subhas Chandra Bose addressed Mahatma Gandhi as the 'Father of the Nation' in a radio broadcast from Rangoon on 6 July 1944 over Azad Hind Radio, seeking his blessings for the INA's fight. (राष्ट्रपिता)

• In the same message he made the famous appeal: 'Father of our Nation, in this holy war for India's liberation, we ask for your blessings and good wishes.'

• Gandhi in turn gave Bose the title 'Netaji', and Bose is remembered for the slogan 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rabindranath Tagore gave Gandhi the title 'Mahatma'; Gandhi called Tagore 'Gurudev'.

• Jawaharlal Nehru described Gandhi's death with the words 'the light has gone out of our lives'; Nehru himself was called 'Chacha Nehru'.

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was given the title 'Sardar' by the women of Bardoli after the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928); he is the Iron Man of India.

NOTE

• Other titles: Lokmanya — B. G. Tilak; Deshbandhu — C. R. Das; Punjab Kesari — Lala Lajpat Rai; Frontier Gandhi — Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan; Rajaji — C. Rajagopalachari.

• Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's birth anniversary, 23 January, is observed as Parakram Diwas since 2021.

question: Oxides of ______ and ______ dissolve in rain water and form acids which is called as acid rain.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sulphur, nitrogen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Acid rain is formed when oxides of sulphur (SO₂, SO₃) and nitrogen (NO, NO₂) dissolve in rain water to form sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) and nitric acid (HNO₃). (अम्लीय वर्षा)

• Rain is called acidic when its pH falls below 5.6 (normal rain is slightly acidic due to dissolved CO₂ forming carbonic acid).

• These oxides come mainly from burning of fossil fuels in thermal power plants, vehicles and smelters.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Phosphorus oxides are not a major air pollutant of rain water; excess phosphates instead cause eutrophication in water bodies.

• Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases causing global warming, not the chief acid-rain agents.

• Calcium and magnesium oxides are basic (alkaline) and actually neutralise acidity.

NOTE

• Acid rain effects: 'marble cancer' of the Taj Mahal (calcium carbonate reacting with acid), corrosion of metals, loss of soil nutrients and death of aquatic life.

• The Mathura Oil Refinery emissions were a major concern for the Taj; the Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) was created for its protection.

question: Satyajit Ray was honoured with Bharat Ratna in 1992. He was a famous ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Filmmaker.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Satyajit Ray (1921–1992) was a legendary Indian filmmaker (director), writer, illustrator and music composer from Bengal, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1992. (फ़िल्मकार)

• His debut film 'Pather Panchali' (1955) and its sequels *Aparajito* and *Apur Sansar* form the celebrated Apu Trilogy.

• In 1992 he also received an Honorary Academy Award (Oscar) for Lifetime Achievement, the only Indian filmmaker to be so honoured.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Physicist Bharat Ratna awardees include C. V. Raman (1954) and A. P. J. Abdul Kalam (1997, aerospace scientist).

• Sachin Tendulkar (2014) is the only cricketer and the youngest recipient of the Bharat Ratna.

• Ray also created the fictional detective Feluda and the scientist Professor Shonku in Bengali literature.

NOTE

• The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in cinema; Ray received it in 1984.

• Other Ray classics: Charulata, Jalsaghar, Mahanagar, Shatranj Ke Khilari, Goopy Gyne Bagha Byne.

question: PM SVANidhi Scheme aims to empower ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Street Vendors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PM SVANidhi stands for Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi, launched on 1 June 2020 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. (रेहड़ी-पटरी विक्रेता — street vendor)

• It provides collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors hit by the COVID-19 lockdown — ₹10,000 in the first tranche, then ₹20,000 and ₹50,000 on timely repayment.

• Benefits include an interest subsidy of 7% and cashback incentives for digital transactions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• BPL families are covered by schemes like Antyodaya Anna Yojana and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana.

• Pregnant women are supported by Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) and Janani Suraksha Yojana.

• Small businesses are financed under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun).

NOTE

• Street vendors' rights are protected by the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014.

• 'SVANidhi se Samriddhi' is the component that links vendors' families to other central welfare schemes.

question: ______ is the female reproductive part of the flower.
solution_text:
The correct answer is pistil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pistil (carpel/gynoecium) is the female reproductive part of a flower. (स्त्रीकेसर)

• It has three parts — stigma (receives pollen), style (tube through which the pollen tube grows) and ovary (contains ovules that become seeds).

• After fertilisation the ovary develops into the fruit and the ovules develop into seeds.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The stamen (androecium) is the male part, made of the anther (produces pollen grains) and the filament (stalk holding the anther).

• Filament and anther are therefore parts of the male reproductive organ, not the female.

• Sprouting is the germination of a seed, not a floral part.

NOTE

• Four whorls of a typical flower: calyx (sepals), corolla (petals), androecium (stamens), gynoecium (carpels).

• A flower with both stamens and pistil is bisexual (e.g. mustard, hibiscus); with only one it is unisexual (e.g. papaya, maize).

question: Which of the following was an ambassador of Persian ruler and was sent to Vijayanagara?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abdur Razzaq.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Abdur Razzaq was a Persian ambassador sent by the Timurid ruler Shah Rukh of Herat to South India; he visited Vijayanagara in 1443 during the reign of Deva Raya II. (फ़ारसी राजदूत)

• He described the splendour of the capital in his account 'Matla-us-Sadain wa Majma-ul-Bahrain', calling the city unparalleled in the world.

• The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty, with its capital at Hampi on the Tungabhadra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nicolo de Conti — an Italian traveller who visited Vijayanagara around 1420 during Deva Raya I.

• Duarte Barbosa — a Portuguese traveller/writer who visited during Krishnadeva Raya's period.

• Fernao Nuniz — a Portuguese horse trader and chronicler who visited during Achyuta Deva Raya's reign.

NOTE

• Other foreign visitors: Domingo Paes (Portuguese, Krishnadeva Raya), Athanasius Nikitin (Russian, Bahmani kingdom), Ibn Battuta (Moroccan, Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq).

• The Battle of Talikota (1565) led to the decline of the Vijayanagara Empire.

question: He is also known as the God of ghatam. Who is ‘He’ in the preceding line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is T H Vinayakram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• T. H. Vinayakram (Vikku Vinayakram) is a Carnatic percussionist celebrated as the 'God of Ghatam'. (घटम — clay-pot percussion instrument)

• The ghatam is an earthen pot used as a percussion (ghana vadya) instrument in Carnatic music, played by striking with fingers, palms and wrists.

• He won a Grammy Award in 1991 as a member of Mickey Hart's 'Planet Drum', and received the Padma Shri (1982) and Padma Bhushan (2014).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ustad Bismillah Khan — shehnai maestro, Bharat Ratna 2001.

• Pandit Ravi Shankar — sitar maestro, Bharat Ratna 1999.

• Ustad Bundu Khan — a renowned sarangi player.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs often asked: Tabla — Zakir Hussain; Sarod — Amjad Ali Khan; Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; Flute — Hariprasad Chaurasia; Mridangam — Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman; Veena — S. Balachander.

• Instrument classes: Tata (string), Sushira (wind), Avanaddha (membrane), Ghana (solid, e.g. ghatam, jaltarang).

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions the fundamental duty “to safeguard public property and to abjure violence”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A (i).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A(i) lays down the fundamental duty 'to safeguard public property and to abjure violence'. (सार्वजनिक संपत्ति की रक्षा और हिंसा से दूर रहना)

• Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IV-A, Article 51A, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• Originally 10 duties were added; the 11th duty (51A(k)) — providing education to children aged 6–14 — was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• 51A(a) — to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals, institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

• 51A(d) — to defend the country and render national service when called upon.

• 51A(g) — to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by courts, and were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• Fundamental Rights — Part III (Articles 12–35); Directive Principles — Part IV (Articles 36–51); Fundamental Duties — Part IV-A (Article 51A).

question: Which ruler defeated Humayun in the battle of Chausa and Kannauj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sher Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sher Shah Suri (Farid Khan) defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun in the Battle of Chausa (26 June 1539) and again in the Battle of Kannauj/Bilgram (17 May 1540). (चौसा एवं कन्नौज का युद्ध)

• After Kannauj, Humayun fled India and Sher Shah founded the Sur Empire (1540–1555) with its capital at Delhi.

• Humayun regained the throne in 1555 after the Battle of Sirhind, with Persian help.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Islam Shah Suri was Sher Shah's son and successor (1545–1554), not the victor of these battles.

• Ali Adil Shah II and Muhammad Adil Shah were rulers of the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur (Deccan), unrelated to Humayun's defeats.

NOTE

• Sher Shah's reforms: the silver Rupiya and copper Dam, the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam), sarais, an efficient land revenue (zabti/ryotwari-type) system and the dak (postal) service.

• His tomb is at Sasaram, Bihar; he also built the Purana Qila and Rohtasgarh Fort.

question: When was the Champaran Agrarian Law passed by the British Government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1918.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Champaran Agrarian Act was passed in 1918, following the report of the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee on which Mahatma Gandhi served as a member. (चंपारण कृषि अधिनियम, 1918)

• The Act abolished the oppressive tinkathia system, under which peasants of Champaran (Bihar) were forced to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land for European planters.

• It also provided for the refund of a part of the illegal enhancements taken by the planters from the ryots.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was Gandhi's first satyagraha in India; he went there at the request of Rajkumar Shukla.

• 1919 is remembered for the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919).

• 1916 saw the Lucknow Pact and the Home Rule Movement.

NOTE

• Gandhi's early Indian movements: Champaran (1917) — indigo planters; Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) — first hunger strike; Kheda (1918) — first non-cooperation experiment.

• Associates at Champaran: Rajendra Prasad, Brajkishore Prasad, J. B. Kripalani, Mahadev Desai, Anugrah Narayan Sinha.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major tribe of South India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dang (Dangi) is associated with the Dang district of southern Gujarat in western India, not with South India. Hence it is the odd one out. (दांग — गुजरात)

• The other three — Toda, Badaga and Irula — are well-known tribes of the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil Nadu in South India.

• The Toda are famous for their buffalo-based pastoral economy, barrel-vaulted huts called 'munds' and embroidered shawl 'putukuli'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Badaga — the largest community of the Nilgiris, mainly agriculturists.

• Irula — a Scheduled Tribe of Tamil Nadu/Kerala, traditionally snake-catchers and honey gatherers.

• Other Nilgiri tribes: Kota, Kurumba and Paniyan.

NOTE

• Major tribes by state: Gond & Bhil — Madhya Pradesh; Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Ho — Jharkhand; Toda, Badaga, Irula, Kota — Tamil Nadu; Chenchu — Andhra Pradesh; Jarawa, Onge, Sentinelese, Great Andamanese, Shompen — Andaman & Nicobar.

• Gond is the largest tribe of India by population; the Bhil are the second largest.
